defect.evidence_quote: Petitioners maintain that even though they may have violated the Fourth Amendment rights of respondents, they are entitled to the defense of qualified immunity. We agree.
defect.problem: The Qualified Immunity home is supported, but the role label 'Key — Progeny / Refinement' is not quite supportable as framed. The disclosed evidence characterizes Hanlon as a same-day companion applying Wilson, not as ordinary progeny.
defect.proposed_fix: Change role to 'Key — Companion / Application' or 'Key — Qualified Immunity Application'.

reasons: The opinion squarely turns on qualified immunity.
The lake treatment scope note says: 'Per curiam companion to Wilson v. Layne; good law.'
residual_risks: No disclosed taxonomy definition explains whether 'Progeny / Refinement' includes same-day companion applications.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Use a companion/application role label rather than progeny/refinement.

defect.evidence_quote: Review of the complaint's much more detailed allegations to the same effect satisfies us that respondents alleged a Fourth Amendment violation under our decision today in Wilson v. Layne, ante, p. 603.
defect.problem: The holding overstates the Fourth Amendment portion by saying the ride-along 'violated' the Fourth Amendment. The opinion text more carefully says the complaint allegations stated or alleged a Fourth Amendment violation under Wilson, then resolved the case on qualified-immunity grounds.
defect.proposed_fix: Revise to: 'The complaint allegations about a media ride-along during execution of the ranch/outbuilding warrant stated a Fourth Amendment violation under Wilson v. Layne, but the officers were entitled to qualified immunity.'

reasons: Qualified immunity is directly supported by the opinion: 'We agree' that petitioners were entitled to qualified immunity.
The Fourth Amendment proposition is supported only at the narrower alleged/stated-violation level.
residual_risks: The holding should avoid implying final merits liability beyond the Court's stated alleged/stated-violation posture.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Use 'stated a Fourth Amendment violation' rather than 'violated the Fourth Amendment'.
